meta.title: Nanobody–Influenza A HA Docking Screening Data
meta.note: This file is the single data source for the Model page's body tables and interactive demo. Values are transcribed entry by entry from modeling document §5.3 / §5.4 / §6, without secondary conversion.
meta.kindNote: All are computational predictions from molecular docking and simulation; modeling document §9 explicitly states 'no experimental validation.' The page must not present them as verified conclusions.
meta.antigenRoleNote: The specificity index is built from the score difference between the target subtype H1N1 and the control subtypes H3N2 and H5N1; the control subtypes are used to quantify specificity, not as detection targets.

cluspro.label: ClusPro rigid docking
cluspro.unit: kcal/mol (the document does not state the unit; only values are given)
cluspro.note: The Top 10 conformations are retained for each 'candidate × antigen' combination.

specificityIndex.label: Specificity index
specificityIndex.note: A more negative value indicates better specificity for H1N1.

haddock.label: HADDOCK 2.5 semi-flexible refinement
haddock.flow: Rigid docking it0 → semi-flexible refinement it1 → water refinement itw
haddock.note: A more negative HADDOCK score indicates better interface quality.

verdict.zh: Best H1N1 specificity (untreated-antigen index −93.25), lowest HADDOCK score (−93.2), stable MD, moderate cross-reactivity risk, MM-GBSA binding free energy −3.74 kcal/mol. The document therefore selects it as the recognition element.
verdict.en: Lead candidate: best H1N1 specificity (−93.25 untreated-antigen index), lowest HADDOCK score (−93.2), stable MD, moderate cross-reactivity, MM-GBSA ΔG = −3.74 kcal/mol.

verdict.zh: Second-best HADDOCK score (−89.4), but the ClusPro specificity index is positive (+23.75); it has the lowest cross-reactivity risk yet poor H1N1 specificity.
verdict.en: Second-best HADDOCK score (−89.4) but positive ClusPro specificity index (+23.75): lowest cross-reactivity risk yet poor H1N1 specificity.

verdict.zh: Third-best HADDOCK score (−84.6), but the ClusPro specificity index is weaker (−40.75) and the cross-reactivity risk is the highest.
verdict.en: Third by HADDOCK score (−84.6); weaker ClusPro specificity index (−40.75) and the highest cross-reactivity risk.

verdict.zh: Mid-range ClusPro specificity index (−57.35), fourth HADDOCK score (−71.1), higher cross-reactivity risk.
verdict.en: Rejected: mid-range specificity index (−57.35), fourth HADDOCK score (−71.1), higher cross-reactivity risk.

verdict.zh: Second-best ClusPro specificity index (−72.55), but the worst HADDOCK score (−68.8), indicating poor interface quality.
verdict.en: Rejected: second-best specificity index (−72.55) but worst HADDOCK score (−68.8), indicating poor interface quality.

interface.method: PyMOL interface analysis (residues) + SPICE interaction analysis (interaction-type counts)

haSide.note: The original document records 'HA side: 30 residues (27–32, 44–53, 303–332, 358–396).'

interface.hotspotNote: ARGB:31 participates in 4 hydrogen bonds; it is the hotspot residue proposed by the document and is written as a target for the subsequent R31A mutant study.

structureGap.zh: The project's own R1aB6–H1N1 docked complex is not published: the HADDOCK export files contain no antibody chain (of 113 complex files, all hold only the HA receptor or a duplicated receptor, never the nanobody). The 3D panel shows the selected candidate's predicted nanobody structure (from structure prediction, single chain) or the antigen source structure (RCSB 9VH4 etc.); both are single components, no binding pose is shown, and neither is our docking complex.
structureGap.en: The project's own R1aB6–H1N1 docked complex is not published: the HADDOCK export files contain no antibody chain (of 113 complex files, all hold only the HA receptor or a duplicated receptor, never the nanobody). The 3D panel shows the selected candidate's predicted nanobody structure (from structure prediction, single chain) or the antigen source structure (RCSB 9VH4 etc.); both are single components, no binding pose is shown, and neither is our docking complex.

md.reportedDuration: 10 ns (per the document body; see caveats)
md.caveat: In source document Figure 5, the RMSD horizontal axis only reaches about 8 ns and the curve peak is about 0.70 nm, inconsistent with the body text '10 ns / 0.45 nm stable'; the page body follows the document's stated values, and the discrepancy is recorded in the page source comments (numbered MQ-6).

mmgbsa.note: Document §9 states: MM-GBSA is based on only 10 frames, with large statistical error.

pipeline.question: Does the processed antigen affect binding?
Does it cross-react with unrelated viruses?
Is the complex stable in water?

limitations: In ClusPro the receptor is treated as rigid, which may miss induced-fit effects.
Docking uses implicit solvent and ignores explicit water bridges.
In HADDOCK the interface is semi-flexible, allowing side-chain rearrangement while the backbone stays fixed.
10 ns of MD may fail to capture slow conformational changes.
MM-GBSA is based on only 10 frames, with large statistical error.
The entire text has no experimental validation (document §9 states this).

reproducibility.value: The document says 'uploaded to GitHub (mdp_files/),' but the repository link is still to be filled in the document.

designDecisions.prediction: R1aB6 has the highest H1N1 specificity

designDecisions.decision: Proposed the R31A mutant as a target for subsequent studies

designDecisions.prediction: R2bD9 and R2bE8 have higher cross-reactivity risk

openItems.zh: Candidate naming has two conventions (R1aXA5/R2bXD9 vs R1aA5/R2bD9). The page uniformly uses the X-less form; the other is pending lab verification.
In the document, the GitHub links for the code repository, parameter files, and input/output structures are all 'to be filled'; the page states the actual status.
MD duration and RMSD: body text 10 ns / 0.45 nm; source-figure trajectory about 8 ns, peak about 0.70 nm.

The source document's two 17-antibody charts (post-processed antigen, cross-reactivity) have candidate-number cross-reference tables inconsistent with the screening figure, so those two charts are not cited; the related results are presented only in tables.
